name: Brian F. Sullivan
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman & CEO, Celcuity Inc. (Nasdaq: CELC), Minneapolis
profile: Serial Minnesota med-tech founder: co-founded filtration firm Recovery Engineering (sold to P&G for $265M, 1999), then ran Sterilmed (sold to J&J for $330M, 2011). Co-founded Celcuity in 2012, took it public in 2017; in July 2026 the FDA approved its first drug, Revtorpyk (gedatolisib), for advanced HR+/HER2- breast cancer.
interesting_fact: Revtorpyk (approved July 14, 2026) is the first FDA-approved drug to inhibit all class I PI3K isoforms plus mTORC1/mTORC2; in Phase 3 VIKTORIA-1 the triplet gave 9.3 months median PFS vs 2.0 months for fulvestrant.
deep_cut_fact: Before biotech he built a water-filtration business (Recovery Engineering) that he took public and sold to Procter & Gamble; he holds 11 U.S. patents and graduated magna cum laude with distinction in economics from Harvard College.

public_contacts.value: Sam Brown LLC - Laura Morgan, lauramorgan@sambrown.com

notes: Sullivan lists himself as an investor contact in Celcuity press releases (published email). Biotech, not energy, but a strong serial-founder story. Not to be confused with Brian F. Sullivan of Entegris.

name: Guo Hongsheng
current_role: Founder of Shenyang Blue Silver (SBS) Group / Blue Silver Industry Automation Equipment (SZSE: 300293); Managing Director & Group CEO, SBS Ecoclean Group (Germany)
profile: Shenyang-born (1962) engineer-entrepreneur who founded the SBS Group in 1996, building Shenyang Blue Silver Industry Automation Equipment (tyre/rubber-processing automation, digital factory systems) into a Shenzhen-listed company. In 2017 he bought Dürr AG's industrial cleaning & surface-processing business, now SBS Ecoclean, which he runs from Germany as Group CEO.
interesting_fact: A Chinese automation founder who personally runs a German Mittelstand engineering group: SBS took majority control of Dürr Ecoclean (founded 1956, Filderstadt) on 1 April 2017 and he has been its Group CEO since.
deep_cut_fact: He founded the SBS Group in 1996 under the motto "technology drives the future" - a line Ecoclean still prints in his official management bio.
notes: Name spellings vary (Guo Hongsheng / Hongsheng Guo / Hong Sheng Guo). Best route is probably via SBS Ecoclean in Germany (English-language corporate comms) rather than the Shenyang listed company. Industrial cleaning for EV/battery and hydrogen components could be a podcast angle.

name: Zhang Tongsheng
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, C&U Co., Ltd. (人本股份) and controlling shareholder of C&U Group (人本集团), Wenzhou
profile: Wenzhou entrepreneur who co-founded the Wenzhou Bearing Factory in 1991 with three partners; it became C&U Group, China's largest bearing maker, plus the Renben (人本) supermarket and Shizu retail chains. He controls ~60.8% of the votes of C&U Co., which re-filed for a Shanghai main-board IPO in late 2025.
interesting_fact: C&U has ranked No.1 in China by bearing output and sales every year since 2013 and is described as the only Chinese company in the global top 10 bearing makers; it employs ~19,000 people.
deep_cut_fact: He started the bearing business at age 24 with a junior-middle-school education; the Wenzhou Bearing Factory was registered in July 1991 with RMB 4 million of capital, and he has led it as chairman ever since.
notes: Low public profile; little personal press. Route via C&U corporate office or the IPO sponsor/IR once listed. Bearings for wind turbines/EVs could be an energy angle.

name: Shen Jinhao
current_role: Founder and former chairman (2005-2019) of Nanfang Pump / Nanfang Zhongjin Environment (SZSE: 300145); reported as chairman of Hangzhou Nanfang Haoyuan Pump Industry
profile: Hangzhou entrepreneur behind CNP (Nanfang Pump), founded 1991 and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in December 2010; it grew into one of China's leading stainless-steel multistage centrifugal pump makers and was renamed Nanfang Zhongjin Environment in 2016 as it expanded into environmental services. He chaired the listed company until 2019; family member Shen Jieyong shares the Hurun listing.
interesting_fact: CNP was among the first batch of companies on Shenzhen's ChiNext-era growth listings (listed 9 Dec 2010, code 300145) and later bought Texas pump maker Tigerflow Systems (2016).
notes: Very little personal coverage; current role after 2019 control change not confirmed from primary filings. Alive status not confirmed (no reports of death found). CNP is now run by a different CEO (Shen Haijun).

name: Gu Qingwei
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Beijing Dinghan Technology Group (鼎汉技术, SZSE: 300011)
profile: Born 1972, a Jiangxi University of Finance & Economics graduate who spent 1996-2002 in Huawei's finance organisation before founding Dinghan in 2002. Dinghan makes rail-transit power systems (signal, platform-door and traction power supplies, train electrical equipment) and was among the first ChiNext listings (2009). Guangzhou state investor GIIC's capital arm is now controlling shareholder; Gu remains chairman and a 5%+ holder.
interesting_fact: Dinghan carries code 300011 - it was in the very first batch of 28 companies to list on Shenzhen's ChiNext board in October 2009; it supplies power systems for metro and high-speed rail across China.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Dinghan he was a Huawei finance man for six years: section chief in finance management, CFO of Shandong Huawei, director of Huawei's Beijing financial shared-services centre and CFO of North Huawei. He holds EMBAs from both Peking and Tsinghua universities.
notes: Good energy/power-electronics angle (rail power supply). Board secretary office (ir@) is the formal route. Source is Dinghan 2024 annual report (bio section).

name: Anstalt Winder
current_role: Not a person: Liechtenstein Anstalt (Winder Anstalt) in a holding chain with Winder Investment Pte Ltd, Freemont Capital Pte Ltd (Singapore) and the Haldor Foundation (Schaan, Liechtenstein); 10%+ holder of Sensient Technologies (SXT)
profile: An investment vehicle, not an individual. SEC 13G filings show the Winder/Freemont/Haldor group built a stake in food-colour and flavour maker Sensient Technologies from 5% (March 2021) to ~14.9-15%; a 2026 filer snapshot shows ~9.8%. Filings are signed by directors William Lexmond and Iqbal Jumabhoy; the ultimate beneficial owner is not named.
interesting_fact: The stake is held through a Singapore family-office-style structure (Freemont Capital, 6 Battery Road) sitting on top of a Liechtenstein foundation - a typical private-wealth wrapper whose beneficiary is not disclosed in SEC filings.
notes: Entity, not a person - recommend dropping from outreach list or researching the beneficial owner separately. Only published route is the registered business address in SEC filings (Freemont Capital Pte Ltd, Singapore); no published email.

name: Jiang Yong
current_role: Director (since 2007) and co-controlling shareholder of Guizhou Bailing Group Pharmaceutical (贵州百灵, SZSE: 002424); former VP (2007-2021)
profile: Born 1968, Jiang Yong is the brother and concert party of Bailing founder Jiang Wei; together they control Guizhou Bailing, an Anshun-based maker of Miao ethnic-minority traditional medicines. He was previously deputy director of the Anshun Pharmaceutical Factory and VP of several Bailing companies, overseeing sales.
interesting_fact: Bailing specialises in Miao (Hmong) ethnic medicine from Guizhou - a niche of Chinese traditional pharmacy rooted in the province's minority communities.
notes: CAUTION: In 2026 the CSRC found Bailing's 2019-2023 annual reports misstated; Jiang Yong (as director/VP) was warned and fined RMB 2M and Jiang Wei resigned as chairman (March 2026). Not a suitable or easy outreach target; poor podcast fit. Company now trades as ST Bailing.

name: Sam Houser
current_role: Co-founder & President, Rockstar Games (Take-Two Interactive), New York
profile: London-born (1971) co-founder of Rockstar Games, set up in New York in December 1998 after Take-Two bought BMG Interactive. As Rockstar's creative chief he has steered Grand Theft Auto, Red Dead Redemption, Max Payne and Bully; GTA V is one of the best-selling entertainment products ever. Now leading development of Grand Theft Auto VI.
interesting_fact: Rockstar was born from BMG's games unit: BMG Interactive had sprawled to offices in about 27 countries ('including Ecuador'), and after BMG sold it to Take-Two in 1998 Sam and Dan Houser moved to New York to found Rockstar.
deep_cut_fact: His own CV: left school in 1989 with 'bad A-level results', re-sat them in 1990, and started a summer job sorting mail at BMG Records in London; through university (1991-94) he worked part-time at BMG on pop videos and VHS releases before moving into BMG Interactive.

public_contacts.value: Alan.Lewis@take2games.com (Take-Two Head of Global Corporate Communications)

notes: Famously press-shy; almost never gives interviews and has no public social accounts. Only realistic route is Take-Two corporate communications. Shares the Rich List entry with brother Dan Houser (who left Rockstar in 2020).

name: Fu Sheng
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Cheetah Mobile (NYSE: CMCM); Chairman, OrionStar (猎户星空) AI & robotics
profile: Born 1978 in Jingdezhen, Jiangxi. Led Qihoo 360's 360 Safeguard team (2005-08), founded Conew Image in 2009, and in 2010 merged it with Kingsoft Security (backed by Lei Jun) to form what became Cheetah Mobile, listed in New York in 2014. Since 2016 he has pivoted to AI via OrionStar, which builds service robots and LLMs and became a Cheetah subsidiary in December 2023.
interesting_fact: Before Cheetah he was the product lead behind 360 Safeguard (360安全卫士), the free security app that made Qihoo 360 one of China's biggest internet companies; he left in 2008 over differences with Zhou Hongyi, and the two publicly reconciled in 2024.
deep_cut_fact: His first brush with the internet was in 1999 as head of the e-commerce department at Xiamen computer maker Xoceco (厦华电脑), followed by enterprise full-text search work at Guoxin Base and a director role at 3721 (later bought by Yahoo China).
notes: Highly public and media-friendly (frequent speaker and short-video creator on AI). Strong fit for an AI/compute angle via OrionStar. Name sometimes rendered 'Sheng Fu'.

name: Lin Guangrong
current_role: Chairman, Shanghai Rotai Health Technology (荣泰健康, SSE: 603579)
profile: Founder-chairman (now about 80) of Rotai, a Shanghai massage-chair maker whose brand dates from 1997 (company incorporated 2002). Rotai listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in January 2017 and makes smart massage chairs, massagers and pads for China and export markets; it is rated a national 'specialised and sophisticated little giant'.
interesting_fact: Rotai massage chairs were the official reception chairs at the 2008 (29th) Beijing Olympic Games, an honour the company still lists in its profile.
notes: Elderly, low-profile founder; board secretary Zhang Bo is the formal route. Weak fit for energy/data-centre themes.

name: Shi Mingtai
current_role: Non-independent director (since June 2026) and No.4 shareholder (~2.4%) of Bear Electric Appliance (小熊电器, SZSE: 002959)
profile: Born 1969, a senior engineer with a master's degree who built his career in State Grid's IT arm rather than in appliances; he is a long-standing major individual shareholder of Bear Electric, the Foshan maker of 'cute' small kitchen appliances founded in 2006 and listed in 2019, and joined its board in 2026.
interesting_fact: Unusually for a consumer-appliance billionaire, his day job was in power-grid IT: he was GM of Xiamen Yili Geo-Information Technology and deputy GM of State Grid Info & Telecom Yili Technology (2012-17).
deep_cut_fact: From 2017 to 2021 he chaired Beijing State Grid Xintong Accenture Information Technology, the State Grid ICT joint venture with Accenture.
notes: Identity matched on name + Bear shareholding + board seat; bio comes from Bear's director disclosure via Eastmoney F10. Grid-IT background makes him a possible energy/digital-grid guest. Bear's founder/controller is Li Yifeng.

name: Shen Jun
current_role: Founder & Chairman, East Money Information (东方财富, SZSE: 300059), Shanghai - known publicly by his pen name Qi Shi (其实)
profile: Shen Jun, better known by the pen name Qi Shi, founded Eastmoney in Shanghai in January 2005 and listed it on ChiNext in March 2010 (when Hurun first listed him under his birth name). Eastmoney grew from a financial portal and stock forum (Guba) into an online brokerage and fund-distribution giant (Tiantian Fund, Choice data), making him one of China's richest fintech founders.
interesting_fact: In 2015 Eastmoney became the first ChiNext company to pass RMB 100bn market cap, and on 9 Oct 2024 its stock traded over RMB 90bn in one day - a single-stock turnover record for China's A-share market.
deep_cut_fact: He runs one of China's largest listed fintechs under a pen name: Wikipedia's Eastmoney entry lists the chairman as '沈军（笔名：其实）' - 'Shen Jun (pen name: Qi Shi)'.
notes: Likely DUPLICATE of the 'Qi Shi' (其实) profile elsewhere in the dataset - 2010 Hurun listing under birth name; today's net worth is far larger. Very private, rarely interviewed. Identity link (Shen Jun = Qi Shi) rests on Chinese Wikipedia, which flags the article as needing sources.

current_role: Major individual shareholder (~7.6%) of Beijing Dahao Technology (大豪科技, SSE: 603025); current executive title not confirmed
profile: One of the founding technical-management shareholders of Beijing Dahao Technology, whose roots go back to 1986 and which makes industrial CNC electronic control systems for sewing and knitting machines; it listed in Shanghai in 2015 and is controlled by state-owned Beijing Yiqing Holdings. He remains the joint-fourth-largest holder with ~7.6% as of Sept 2026.
interesting_fact: Dahao's control systems sit inside a large share of China's industrial sewing and knitting machines - an unglamorous but dominant niche of Chinese CNC electronics, run from Beijing's Jiuxianqiao electronics park.
notes: Shareholding confirmed from Eastmoney top-10 holders (Q3 2026); personal bio not found (search budget exhausted). Very low profile.

name: Sun Yizheng
current_role: Co-founder and joint actual controller (with Zhang Wan) of Yimikang Technology Group (依米康, SZSE: 300249), Chengdu; ~5.3% direct holder
profile: Co-founded Sichuan Yimikang Refrigeration in 2002 with Zhang Wan (the Hurun entry's 'Zhang Yuan' is 张菀); they jointly control 20.7% of what is now Yimikang Technology Group, listed on ChiNext in 2011. The company makes precision cooling and thermal-management equipment for data centres and now sells full-lifecycle 'green digital infrastructure' and zero-carbon data-centre solutions.
interesting_fact: Yimikang bills itself as the first A-share-listed company in China's precision-environment/data-centre cooling industry, and now positions itself around zero-carbon data centres.
notes: STRONG podcast fit (data-centre cooling / green digital infrastructure). Co-founder Zhang Wan is the current chairman and the more visible face of the company - she may be the better guest. Sun no longer holds a listed management title per current disclosures.
